thread:
support-liaison: heads up — PulseAI is reporting ~20% 503s for hosted ingestion endpoints for the last 25m. They opened ticket #PL-1987 and are pretty upset about SLA impacts. logs attached show upstream worker exits. :grimacing:

gpu-oncall: looking now. can you paste a sample request id and the error from the runner logs?

support-liaison: request id 01H8K2C4XJ9, customer trace: 
```
2026-03-17T12:08:45Z runner[pid=2112]: inference_worker: unhandled signal 4 (Illegal instruction)
2026-03-17T12:08:45Z runner[pid=2112]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f9c1b2e3d4f sp 00007ffda2b1f370 error 4 in libcutlass.so
2026-03-17T12:08:45Z docker: container exit code 132
```

support-liaison: another sample shows GPU OOM just before crash: 
```
E Cuda out of memory trying to allocate 3.6 GiB
W Prefetcher: dropping prefetch for context=ctx-77
```

ajay: hmm illegal instruction & OOM together — could be a quantized kernel hitting unsupported op on this driver. which model variant were they hitting?

support-liaison: model id redwood/open-3b-q4_0, region us-west-2, traffic routed through hosted pool `hw-pool-14`. Spike started after a canary swap 11:30 PDT (auto quant swap).

maria: pinging infra — did we roll any driver/kernel updates in us-west-2 this morning?

infra-bot: deployment-notice: GPU driver rollout started 2026-03-17T08:00 UTC in us-west-2, 18/54 hosts updated. No rollback events reported.

gpu-oncall: ok that explains illegal instruction — older CUDA kernels on some hosts may not support newer cutlass ops used by q4 kernels. but OOMs too could be a separate path (batch size/batching change).

sylvie: customer says errors spike when they include a long context (~12k tokens) + tool-calls, so KV cache prefetch + dynbatch may be inflating memory pressure.

ajay: repro plan: spin up a staging worker with the same driver version and the exact quantized model, run a synthetic replay with long-context requests and toolcall payloads. capture core, nvcrash, and run gdb bt.

maria: steps I ran locally (staging):
```
# reproduce harness (staging)
./run_repro --model redwood/open-3b-q4_0 --context 12000 --concurrency 4 --pack-toolcalls
# capture logs
journalctl -u infer-worker --since "10 minutes ago" > /tmp/repro-journal.log
coredumpctl dump --output=/tmp/core.runner
gdb -batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" /usr/bin/runner /tmp/core.runner > /tmp/backtrace.txt
```

maria: on one staging host I saw identical illegal instruction in libcutlass and then a cuda mem usage spike to 98% before OOM.

gpu-oncall: mitigation for customers: 1) route PulseAI traffic off `hw-pool-14` to `hw-pool-07` (hosts with newer driver) 2) temp pin model->non-quantized variant (open-3b-fp16) 3) reduce dynbatch max_batch to 1 for their route.

support-liaison: PulseAI accepted a short mitigation if we can do routing change quickly. They also asked for ETA to root cause.

ajay: action items:
- infra: pause driver rollout in us-west-2 and mark `hw-pool-14` hosts draining for driver update consistency (infra)
- ops: add a route override for PulseAI to `hw-pool-07` (ops)
- runtime: pin model to fp16 variant and rollback the quant swap in canary (runtime)
- triage: collect core dumps, nvcrash, /proc/driver/nvidia/version, and the exact runner binary SHA (triage)

triage-bot: created ticket /incidents/PL-1987-escalation, assigned to ajay, priority P1, linked to runbook `gpu-oom-sigill-escalation`

ajay: I'll take triage — collecting artifacts now. can ops do the routing?

maria: I can handle route override. will update PulseAI once done.

maria: route override in place, traffic for PulseAI is now on hw-pool-07. monitoring for error rate drop. :white_check_mark:

support-liaison: PulseAI reports errors dropped to <1% after migration. they want a postmortem and assurance this won't recur.

ajay: collecting artifacts: attached gdb backtrace points to cutlass:neon::kernels::matmul_impl +0x1f3, which is consistent with an unsupported SIMD path on older GPUs/drivers. nvcrash captured GPU register dump and ptx assembler mismatch lines.

ajay: quick debug commands I'm running: 
```
# verify driver+cuda
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
# inspect lib cutlass
ldd /usr/lib/libcutlass.so | grep cuda
# run cuda-memcheck on small reproducer
cuda-memcheck ./infer_worker_repro --model redwood/open-3b-q4_0 --context 12000
```

ajay: hypothesis: driver rollout created heterogenous fleet with some hosts on older driver that miscompile/trigger illegal instruction in newer quant kernels; when the prefetch/dynbatch memory spike happens, some paths also OOM and crash. Two independent failures but both exposed by the same canary quant swap.

sylvie: plan for remediation:
- short: keep PulseAI on hw-pool-07 until full fleet driver parity is achieved; rollback canary quant swap to fp16 for hosted pool 14; inform customers.
- medium: add driver-compatibility gate for quantized kernels — runtime should check libcutlass/cuda capability and fallback to fp16 variant if unsupported.
- long: add automated integration test that runs q4 kernels on each driver version in a pool before promos.

infra-bot: driver-rollout: paused by infra@us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T12:30 UTC; 18 hosts updated, 36 pending.

maria: will draft a customer-facing postmortem and timeline. ajay, please tag any kernel/stack frames you want called out.

ajay: attaching short repro notes and core dump links in ticket. marking for follow-up with research/ML to validate quant kernel compatibility matrix.

support-liaison: Customer follow-up scheduled at 2026-03-17T13:15 PDT; they want confirmation that the fleet is stable before we re-enable quantized pool.

gpu-oncall: I'll keep monitoring hw-pool-07 and the paused pool. will also schedule a small canary run for q4 on a single validated host (with full nvprof/cuda checks) once infra confirms driver parity.

support-liaison: thx all — outstanding items: postmortem draft, infra to finish driver parity, runtime guard to detect unsupported kernels. closing loop after canary test passes. :pray:

triage-bot: thread closed for now; reopen if regressions appear.
